Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:82: And so they further expound in Shemot Rabbah (24:1), Parashat "Vayisa" (Exodus 15:22), on the verse (Deuteronomy 32:6), "do you thus repay the LORD," and so on - for it is one of the conditions of children to perform their father's will, and then they are called children and the father performs his children's will; in these words: "is He not your Father, who acquired you" - if you have merited [it, He is] your Father; just as a son endears himself to his father and the father does his will, so you endear yourselves before Him and He does your will.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:83: Another interpretation: if "your Father," why "who acquired you"; if "who acquired you," why "your Father"? Rather, when Israel performs the will of the Omnipresent, He has mercy on them like a father on his children; and when they do not perform His will, He drives them like a servant - just as a servant, whether willingly or unwillingly, serves his master against his will, so you shall perform the will of the Omnipresent, willingly or unwillingly, against your will. Rabbi Tachlifa of Caesarea, in the name of Rabbi Pila, says: come and see how many miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performs for man, and he does not know it - for were he to eat bread while it was still raw [undigested properly], it would descend into his intestines and scratch him, but the Holy One, blessed be He, created a spring [gullet lining] within his throat that brings down the bread in peace. "He made you and established you" - He made you what you need, and after all this, "do you thus repay the LORD" - you go and speak excessive words! To this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:84: Further, among the things arousing love, it is explained in Bamidbar Rabbah, Parashat Nazir, on the verse (Song of Songs 5:16), "his palate is most sweet, and he is altogether desirable [machamadim]" - in these words: "altogether desirable" - Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said: it is the way of the world that a worker does [service] for the householder - by making himself dirty in mud, [only then] he gives him his wage. But the Holy One, blessed be He, warns Israel and says to them: do not make yourselves vile with anything evil, and I will give you your reward - this is what is written (Leviticus 11:43), "do not defile your souls," and so on. What is "I am the LORD"? I am reliable to pay a reward for this - amazing! Behold, "altogether desirable."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:85: Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiya, in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: it is written (Ezekiel 20:20), "and sanctify My Sabbaths" - with what do you sanctify it? With food, drink, and clean clothing. What is written of it? "And they shall be a sign between Me and you, that you may know that I am the LORD your God" - I am the LORD, reliable to pay you a reward for this. Behold, "altogether desirable." "This is my beloved" - as it says (Leviticus 20:26), "and I have separated you from the peoples, to be Mine" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:86: Further, among the things that arouse His love, blessed be He, for us, as mentioned, is that the Shechinah guards us in this exile - as it is written in the Haggadah, "it is this that has stood by our fathers and us," for it was not just one who rose against us, and so on, and the Holy One, blessed be He, saves us from their hand. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say (Yoma, chapter 7, page 69b), that after the Destruction, they sought to eliminate the phrase "the great, mighty, and awesome God"; the Men of the Great Assembly came and restored it, saying: these are His mighty deeds, these are His awesome deeds - that He maintains us among the nations. And it says, great is the Shepherd who guards His flock; and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say (Sotah 9a): "half of them He consumed" - half are destroyed and they are not [entirely] destroyed - and this is what the prophet laments (Lamentations 5:22), "unless You have utterly rejected us, and are very angry with us." And the intent is that had the Holy One, blessed be He, rejected us, His anger would have been to the point of destroying everything - and since we see that the Holy One, blessed be He, left us a remnant, His intent in the exile and destruction was only to chastise us, so that we return in repentance - therefore it says, "turn us to You, O LORD, and we shall return." And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say at the end of Megillat Eichah (Eichah Rabbah 5:20), that one who is angry ultimately becomes reconciled, and so it is said through Isaiah (Isaiah 57:16), "for I will not contend forever, nor will I always be angry."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:87: And the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot, peace be upon him, writes (Gate of Contemplation, chapter 5): and the greatest of the good things He did for man is the Torah given to us through Moses our prophet, and the showing of the signs through him; and if a person seeks, in this time, to see something resembling those matters, let him look with the eye of truth at our standing among the nations from the time of the exile, and the arrangement of our affairs among them, and so on; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:88: And besides this, that He answers us in all our troubles when we consider repentance and regret our sins and fast and repent - immediately the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on us - particularly in the matter of the withholding of rains, this matter is tested in Israel countless times, for Israel is a holy and beloved people before their Creator: when they decree three fasts, they are answered - and through this the Name of Heaven is sanctified and it shows that there is a God for Israel, as the prophet says (Jeremiah 14:22), "are there any among the vanities of the nations who can cause rain? Or can the heavens give showers? Are You not He, O LORD our God? Therefore we will wait for You," and so on. Behold, this aspect of love encompasses all of Israel.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:89: Further, another aspect of love encompasses a portion of the nation of Israel - those who gathered while being dispersed, and returned and took shelter beneath the wings of the Shechinah, for whom the Holy One, blessed be He, performed countless miracles, and they are obligated to give thanks and praise to the Creator - which is what we say every day, "blessed is our God who created us for His honor, and separated us from those who go astray, and gave us the Torah of truth" - and how many souls there were sunk within the depths of the husk! And going out from there is truly comparable to the Exodus from Egypt - and indeed, the essence of our Exodus from Egypt was not [merely] our going out from bodily servitude to redemption, but rather that our souls too were sunk in the husk of these idol-worshippers and these idol-worshippers, as is known from what they explain, of blessed memory (Shemot Rabbah 16:2), "draw out and take" - draw your hands away from idolatry.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:90: And further, there is a general aspect of love that is particular to each and every man according to his own level - when he examines within himself how many miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for him from the day he came to understanding, besides what He did for him in his childhood days; and when the Holy One, blessed be He, does good for him in wisdom, or wealth, or dominion beyond the rest of the people, he is obligated to a particular service to the Creator beyond the general service, more than what the whole nation does. And so the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot writes (Gate of Accepting the Service of God, end of chapter 3), in these words: and when he discerns the goodnesses of the Creator upon him, through which He singled out him and his tribe from the rest of the peoples, he should believe in his obligation regarding the commandments received by tradition, beyond the rest of the nations; and so too, when he discerns the goodness of God upon him, through which He singled out his tribe and his people from the rest of the tribes of his own people, such as the priesthood and the Levites, he should believe in his obligation regarding the commandments through which God singled out his tribe - and therefore you find that the Torah of the priesthood has twenty-four [sections], corresponding to twenty-four goodnesses the Creator bestowed on the priests, which are the twenty-four priestly gifts. And by this analogy, whoever God singles out for good beyond other people must obligate himself to a service that distinguishes him from them, along with his striving in the general service that includes him with them, to the extent of his ability and comprehension, to thank God, blessed be He, for what He singled him out in of good, and it will cause this to continue, and add to it as repayment for his service when it comes - and he should not be like what is said (Hosea 2:10), "and I multiplied her silver and gold, which they made into Baal" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:91: And in chapter 6 he further writes concerning this matter: whoever rebels against God with the goodness through which He singled him out will fall from all his extra virtues, and the Creator will be more exacting with him in reckoning in this world, as it is said (Leviticus 10:3), "this is what the LORD spoke, saying, I will be sanctified in those who are near to Me," and so on, and it says (Amos 3:2), "you only have I known of all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you," and so on - and his punishment in the World to Come will be even harsher, as it is said (Isaiah 30:33), "for Tophet has long been ordained; it too has been prepared for the king," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:92: And he further writes: and whatever additional good the Creator gives to a person, he is obligated in service for it - and the proof of this is that produce is obligated in tithes, as it is said, "you shall surely tithe," and so on; and one to whom God gave a hundred kor is obligated in ten kor from them, and one to whom He gave ten kor is obligated in one kor from them; and if the one gives nine and a half and the other gives one whole kor, the first will be punished and the second will receive reward. And so, one who has no son, the obligation of circumcision and Torah study is exempted from him; and one who is lame, the obligation of the festival pilgrimage is exempted from him; and one who is ill, the commandments he cannot perform are exempted from him - and by this analogy, one whom the Creator, blessed be He, singles out for good is obligated to add service for it. And therefore the early pious ones, when some worldly good came to them, would be fearful of it, for two reasons: one, lest they fall short in completing the service owed for it and the thanksgiving for it, and it turn to evil for them, as Jacob our father, peace be upon him, said (Genesis 32:10), "I am unworthy of all the kindnesses," and so on; and second, lest it be the Creator's repayment for their service, and their reward in the World to Come be diminished - as the ancients explain concerning (Deuteronomy 7:10), "and repays those who hate Him to their face, to destroy them" - to this point, their words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:93: Up to here have arrived the matters of contemplation we found in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, and the commentators, of blessed memory, which a person must discern to know the Creator's love, so that through this he be diligent in his service and fulfill it out of love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:1: Because we have already dealt, in the previous chapters, with the things that arouse love, and we said in the previous chapter that all the miracles performed for us were performed through the Shechinah, as it is written (Deuteronomy 32:6), "do you thus repay the LORD" - and from this we are obligated to arouse love for her - we have seen fit to attach this chapter to it, to explain in several matters why it is fitting that we direct our love toward her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:2: It is already known that we are called children, as it is said (ibid. 14:1), "you are children of the LORD your God"; and it is known that it is the way of a son to strive for his mother's honor, as explained in chapter 3, where they explain, of blessed memory (Kiddushin 31a), that of this it is said (Exodus 20:12), "honor your father and your mother" - that it is the way of a son to honor his mother more, and therefore the verse puts the father first for honor - and this is certainly from the side of love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:3: And the difference between a servant and a son is that a servant sometimes serves in order to receive a reward, but a son does not serve in order to receive a reward, but rather out of love for his father and mother - and so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Kedoshim, page 82a). And there is a son whose soul is from Atzilut, and they say there (page 83a) that a son who is from there does not strive in Torah to receive a reward, not in deed, not in speech, and not in thought - to this point. And likewise, one whose soul is from there, no sin comes by his hand (there).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:4: And although we find Israel also called servants, as it is said (Leviticus 25:55), "for the children of Israel are servants to Me; they are My servants" - it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 223a) that it is from the side of the Shechinah that they are called servants, because she is the one who serves her husband; in these words: three fathers were called servants from her side, in the name of the Shechinah, who is the service of the LORD, and so too Moses is a servant of the LORD, and therefore "for the children of Israel are servants to Me" - but with respect to others, all Israel are sons of kings, from the side of Malchut. And why is she called "service" [avodah]? Like the manner of a wife to serve her husband, and the manner of children to serve their father - to this point. And the intent of this, as we explained above, is that the Shechinah always arouses song, as it says (Psalms 83:2), "O God, do not keep silence; do not hold Your peace" - and she needs, for her own arousal, the arousal of Israel's deeds, who are cleaved to her, and in this aspect they are called servants.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:5: And whoever wishes to cleave to the love of the Shechinah must always arouse deeds toward her, whether Torah or a commandment, in order to arouse toward her "female waters" [mayin nukvin] - and the proof is from Benjamin, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (page 153b), that he is a chariot for the Shechinah in the secret of "female waters," and he leaped into the sea, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Sotah, chapter 5, 37a), on the verse (Psalms 68:28), "there is little Benjamin, their ruler" - in these words: "there is little Benjamin, their ruler [rodem]" - Rabbi Meir would say, at the time Israel crossed the sea, the tribes were competing with one another, this one saying, I will go down first, and that one saying, I will go down first; the tribe of Benjamin leaped and went down into the sea, as it is said, "there is little Benjamin, their ruler [rodem]" - do not read "rodem" but "radim" [descended] - and the princes of Judah were stoning them [rogmim], as it is said, "the princes of Judah, their council [rigmatam]" - therefore Benjamin merited to become the host for the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Deuteronomy 33:12), "and He shall dwell between his shoulders" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:6: And the reason the tribes were competing over who would enter first is that the splitting of the Red Sea required the arousal from below - and this is what the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses (Exodus 14:15), "why do you cry to Me? Speak to the children of Israel, that they go forward" - meaning, that they themselves should begin to enter the sea, indicating their faith that the sea would split for them - and through this arousal, that they begin, the sea would split for them; "and you, lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand over the sea, and divide it." And because the tribe of Benjamin knew the root of their father's soul, which is the source and root for the arousal from below, they therefore began immediately with that desire and leaped into the sea - therefore they merited that the Shechinah be in their portion, namely the Temple, which was built in the portion of Benjamin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:7: And we learn from this matter that whoever wishes the Holy One, blessed be He, to perform a miracle for him, which is a change of nature, must first change his own nature for His service - along the lines of the splitting of the Red Sea, which is a matter outside of nature. And therefore it says in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach, page 52b) that this depends on the Atika, for from there nature, which is "Elohim," changes and turns into mercy - and therefore the tribe of Benjamin needed to do something contrary to nature, leaping into the sea.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:8: And we further learn from this that if even the splitting of the Red Sea, a matter depending on the Atika, required arousal from below - and the Atika is generosity and plain mercy - how much more so was arousal from below needed in matters that depend on the lower attributes, on Ze'ir [Anpin], which is the place of judgment, and on the Nukva, which is the place of judgment in essence, called "Tzedek," judgment that has no generosity at all - certainly from there arousal is always needed, and in her is the essential arousal, as explained concerning the matter of Benjamin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:9: And further, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 244b) that the Shechinah is unified in the secret of the love of union only through the souls of the righteous; in these words: Rabbi Elazar opened and said (Song of Songs 8:6), "set me as a seal upon your heart," and so on - this verse has already been discussed, but there was one night when I stood before my father and heard a matter from him: there is no completeness, desire, and longing of the Community of Israel for the Holy One, blessed be He, except through the souls of the righteous, who arouse the flow of the lower waters toward the upper ones, and at that hour the completeness of desire is in one cleaving, to make fruits - to this point. Behold, since the matter depends on them, it is fitting that they hasten to bind themselves in her love, in order to arouse the supernal love - and through this they are bound to the Shechinah, as explained there further on, that the Shechinah is found between two righteous men, and of this it is said, "the righteous shall inherit the land."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:10: Behold, all this arousal depends on the deeds of the righteous, even at the time the Temple stood - and as explained above in the Gate of Fear, chapter 1, that after the completion of the offering, Israel would be at their stations and the Levites at their song and music, in such a way that the arousal always ascended - how much more so now, in our many sins, in this great and bitter exile, when the Shechinah has no arousal from the deed of the offering, but only a slight support through the deeds of the righteous, who must support her a little from her fall - for she is the fallen Sukkah of David, which falls further every day than the day before - and all this because of our sins, as it says (Isaiah 50:1), "and for your transgressions your mother is sent away" - for through sins she falls, and through deeds she is raised up and given support, as it says in the Zohar (Parashat Shemini, page 40a), in these words: Rabbi Yehuda opened and said (Song of Songs 2:5), "sustain me with raisin cakes, refresh me with apples," and so on - this verse has already been discussed, and well - but the Community of Israel says this in exile: "sustain me" - what is "sustain me"? Rather, whoever falls needs to be supported - this is what is written (Psalms 145:14), "the LORD supports all who fall," and so on - and therefore the Community of Israel, who has fallen, of whom it is written, "she has fallen and shall no more rise" [an allusion, contrasted here], needs support, and she says, "sustain me" - to whom? To Israel, her children, who are in exile with her. "With what? With raisin cakes" - these are the fathers, who were first filled with that good wine that is preserved; and whoever knows how to unify the holy Name, even though blessings are not found in the world, supports and sustains the Community of Israel in exile - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:11: If so, accordingly, since the Shechinah asks of Israel, her children, that they support her - for her support certainly depends on our hands, namely through the unifications in our prayer and our Torah, which are a support and sustenance for her - even though there is no [full] union in exile, we must support her through unification, for through this some illumination comes to her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:12: And my teacher, peace be upon him, would say that this is like the parable of a king who was banished from his kingdom and went into exile - one who does him a kindness, giving him a piece of bread and a jug of water, that small amount would be as precious in the king's eyes as though he had fed him fattened chickens while he stood in his kingdom. And similar to this parable, they say in the Tikkunim (page 146b), in these words: rather, certainly, when the Shechinah is in exile, whoever performs a commandment to raise her from exile is as though he honored the Holy One, blessed be He - like a king who had a quarrel with the Matronita and cast her out of his Heichal, and she went to the house of her neighbor - and behold, whoever receives her into his house and honors her certainly honors the king, and brings peace between her and her husband - behold, whatever honor is done to her is done to the king; for if the king was angry with her once or twice, he will be reconciled with her and return her to his house, and he will ask her, who honored you, or who demeaned you, or if another kingdom drove her out, in a similar manner - to this point. And we will copy the rest below, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:13: And this is the Shechinah's desire, that we always unify her - whether in prayer, whether in the occupation with a commandment, such as acts of loving-kindness and other commandments, whether in the occupation with Torah - and all these aspects are explained in the Zohar and the Tikkunim.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:14: Concerning the matter of prayer, they explain in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 200a), on the verse (Exodus 35:5), "take from among you an offering" - that the "offering" is the Shechinah with her husband, who are "two out of a hundred" - and it says: and when we need to raise this lower female, it is forbidden for us to take her alone, but rather her and her husband, and they are the two out of the hundred we mentioned, because they must not be separated at all, but rather unified, she and her husband - and therefore it is called "terumah" [offering] in one totality. And come and see, every single day a herald calls out - all the people of the world, this matter stands upon you: "take from among you an offering for the LORD" - and should you say this matter is difficult for you, "every one whose heart makes him willing shall bring it" - what is "shall bring it [yeviah]"? From here we learn the secret of a person's prayer, and so on. And they explain there that the whole prayer, with the songs, with the blessings of the Shema and the Amidah, is all a repair for the Shechinah, to unify her - and they elaborate there. And this whole reality of unification depends on the intention of the heart, "every one whose heart makes him willing shall bring it" - meaning, shall bring her up above and unify her - and so it says at the end of the discourse: and therefore happy is he who sets his heart and his will to this - and therefore it is written, "every one whose heart makes him willing shall bring the offering of the LORD" - to the King - "his heart shall bring [it]" to the supernal King, as has been said.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:15: And concerning the matter of the commandments, it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Ki Tetzei, page 281a), in these words: and it is not for nothing that the Holy One, blessed be He, says: one who occupies himself with Torah and acts of loving-kindness and prays with the congregation, I credit him as though he redeemed Me and My children from among the nations. And how many people strive in Torah and perform acts of loving-kindness, and the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah are not redeemed - rather, [it is only credited to] one who strives in Torah to join it with the Holy One, blessed be He; and acts of loving-kindness - they have already established that "chasid" [pious] refers only to one who is kind to his Creator, for all the commandments he performs are to redeem His Shechinah, and in this he performs kindness with the Holy One, blessed be He. Whoever performs kindness with the Holy One, blessed be He, performs it with His Shechinah - because when Israel sinned, and the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to chastise them, the Mother [Shechinah] was crouching over them until they went out to bad character; what did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He drove out the King's son and the Matronita, and He vowed not to return to His place until the Matronita returned to her place. And whoever returns in repentance and performs kindness with the Shechinah, and with all her Torah and her commandments - and this is only to redeem the Shechinah - this one performs kindness with his Creator, and it is as though he redeemed her, His Shechinah, and His children.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:16: Elijah and all the heads of the academies said: faithful shepherd, are you this person? Are you the son of the King and the Matronita, that your striving toward the Holy One, blessed be He, is not like one who performs kindness with his Creator, but rather like a son who is obligated to set himself and his strength to redeem his father and mother, and give himself over to death for them - for whoever is not the King's son and does good with the King and the Matronita, certainly this one is considered as performing kindness with his Creator.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:17: The faithful shepherd arose and prostrated himself before the Holy One, blessed be He, and wept, and said: so may it be His will to consider me a son, that my deeds toward the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah be, in His eyes, like a man who strives on behalf of his father and mother, whom he loves more than himself, his soul, his spirit, and his soul, and all the world that he has - considering them as nothing, in order to perform the will of the father and mother and redeem them through them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:18: And what he says, that all the commandments performed are to redeem the Shechinah through them - the intent of the redemption is her unification, for through her unification she ascends from the exile, which are the husks, and is purified and refined and unified with her husband.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:19: And what he says, "and through this he performs kindness with the Holy One, blessed be He" - because a king without a Matronita is not a [complete] king, and His completeness is with her completeness. And so they say in the Tikkunim (page 146b), in these words, in brief: correspondingly, the Holy One, blessed be He, drove out the Shechinah and cast her out of His house - this is what is written (Isaiah 50:1), "and for your transgressions your mother is sent away" - and is it not that whoever honors her honors the Holy One, blessed be He, or whoever demeans her demeans the Holy One, blessed be He? And therefore, "for those who honor Me I will honor, and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed" - to this point. And it says above this that the honor of the Shechinah is to perform the commandment to raise her from exile, in these words: when the Shechinah is in exile, whoever performs a commandment to raise her from exile is as though he honored the Holy One, blessed be He - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:20: And without doubt, performing a commandment with fear and love gives her ascent and removal from the exile, which is the husks, as it says in the Tikkunim (page 25b): and a commandment without fear and love cannot ascend and stand before the LORD. It follows that the wings that raise her above, so that the husks not seize her, are fear and love, and without them she cannot ascend. And concerning the matter of the occupation with commandments, we will elaborate further on this, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:21: And concerning the matter of who is the pious one who is kind to his Creator, they further explain in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 222b) that the Torah was given from the right side, which is Chesed, and one who occupies himself with Torah for the sake of unification is called "chasid," kind to his Creator; in these words: the Torah was given from the right side of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is Chesed, and therefore one who occupies himself with Torah is called "chasid" - and therefore I say to the Holy One, blessed be He, "guard my soul, for I am pious [chasid]" - and do not judge her like the deeds of these unlearned people, of whom it is said, "an unlearned person cannot be pious." And should you say, how many unlearned people perform kindness? Rather, they have thus established: who is "chasid"? One who is kind to his Creator - such as David, who would join together - and what would he join together? The supernal Torah he would join with the Holy One, blessed be He - and therefore, "guard my soul, for I am pious" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:22: And in the Tikkunim (end of page 1), they further explain concerning this matter, in these words: the pious [chasidim] are from the side of Chesed, the level of Abraham, and they have established of him, "there is no chasid except one who is kind to his Creator" - who makes for Him a nest, which is His lodging - and this is the Shechinah, who is His nest, His house - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:23: It appears to me that these words of his may be understood together with what is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Ki Tetzei, page 276b), in these words: he opened and said, faithful shepherd, this bride of yours, the Holy One, blessed be He, gave her to Abraham to raise her for you, with us - and because he guarded her, she is called his daughter - this is what is written, "he had a daughter, Abraham, and Bakol was her name" [an interpretation reading "bekol" as a proper name] - and through her he fulfilled the entire Torah, even eruvei tavshilin [the rabbinic ordinance of "mixture of dishes"] - this is what is written (Genesis 26:5), "and he kept My charge," and so on - and he was to her like a guardian [foster-father], as in (Esther 2:7), "and he was foster-father [omen] to Hadassah" - and the Holy One, blessed be He, blessed him for her sake - this is what is written (Genesis 24:1), "and the LORD blessed Abraham in all things" - and he raised her with all good attributes, and did kindness with her, and raised her in greatness with the attribute of Abraham's Chesed, and his house was open wide for her sake, to perform kindness with all who come into the world - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:24: We thus learn from this discourse that the essence of the acts of loving-kindness that Abraham our father, peace be upon him, performed is to perform kindness with the Shechinah - and this in two things: the first, that she be included of all the good attributes, and the second, to bind her with Chesed - and his house was open wide to perform kindness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:25: And the explanation that she be included of all the good attributes is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 159b), and it says there that the Shechinah, all six weekdays, goes wandering from place to place to see whether she finds a righteous man to whom she may cleave; and it says afterward, and who is the righteous man to whom she cleaves, who becomes a chariot for the Righteous One, the Living One of the worlds - the one who is included of all the good attributes; and in these words: and who is the righteous man to whom she cleaves? That one who is included of all the attributes of the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom it is said, "and they were finished" [vayechulu] - included of everything, for all the sefirot are included in him - for he is pious and performs kindness with the Shechinah and gives her strength in Gevurah, and so in every single sefirah he gives her strength through him, and she cleaves to him and does not depart from him all six days of the week, and for his sake it is said, "the world stands on account of one righteous man"; and in him, "the wings of the dove covered with silver" (Psalms 68:14) - she covers herself upon him with her wings and shields him from all the accusers of the world - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:26: Behold, it explicitly says that he must be included of all the good attributes among the ten attributes, so that the Shechinah receive from him strength and illumination from every single attribute, for she receives only through the righteous man, and therefore they must be included within him - and this is what it says, "and so in every single sefirah he gives her strength through him." And although only "kind" [gomel chesed] and "mighty" [gibor] are explained here among the ten attributes, he relies on what he explains them elsewhere in the Tikkunim, and we will explain them below, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:27: And concerning the matter of the occupation with Torah to unify the Shechinah, it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 97b), in these words: meanwhile, the faithful shepherd came, taking a stone in his hand. He opened and said: "zarka, makaf, shofar holech, segulta" [a mnemonic of cantillation notes] - he took three stones and cast them upward, and when he cast them, they became one stone; and he said to the masters of the academy: receive this stone among you, for the Shechinah is in exile, and there is none among you who is aroused toward her, to appease her toward her husband. And not only that, but how many masters of study houses who are colleagues among you cry out every day and night in the Oral Torah with several difficult questions, and cry out in it like dogs who say, "give, give" - similar to Gehinnom, which cries out "give, give" - this is what is written (Proverbs 30:15), "the leech has two daughters, 'give, give'" - give us wealth in this world, give us wealth in the World to Come - as they have established (end of Avot 2 [2:16]), "study Torah much and they will give you great reward" - and there is none who strives in Torah to raise the Shechinah from exile and join her with her husband, for their eyes are sealed and their hearts are closed.
